moat_against: Government is the customer — rates set politically, no pricing power, contracts rebid
Medicaid policy headwinds — federal funding cuts and redeterminations; FY2026 Medicaid membership guided -8% to -9%
ACA subsidy expiry — Marketplace membership fell from ~5.9M to 3.5M YoY in Q2 2026
Razor-thin insurer margins — FY2025 HBR 91.9% leaves no buffer against medical-cost spikes
Medical-cost inflation exposure — behavioral health, home health, high-cost drugs, No Surprises Act disputes
moat_for: #1 US Medicaid MCO — largest Medicaid footprint, incumbency across ~29 states in contract rebids
Medicare PDP scale — 8.8M members in Q2 2026 and growing
Lean cost structure — FY2025 adjusted SG&A expense ratio 7.4%
moat_justification: Weak moat. Centene is the largest US Medicaid managed-care organization with incumbency across a ~29-state footprint, the leading ACA Marketplace franchise (Ambetter), and growing Medicare PDP scale (8.8M members in Q2 2026) at a lean 7.4% adjusted SG&A ratio — real scale advantages in government-program procurement. Against that: the customer is the government, rates are set politically and contracts are rebid, so there is no pricing power; Medicaid federal funding cuts and redeterminations are shrinking the rolls (FY2026 Medicaid membership guided down 8-9%); ACA enhanced-subsidy expiry already cut Marketplace membership from ~5.9M to 3.5M YoY; and insurer margins are razor-thin (FY2025 HBR 91.9%), leaving earnings hostage to medical-cost inflation in behavioral health, home health and high-cost drugs. Morningstar assigns managed-care names at most a narrow moat and Centene none — consistent with a weak 4/10.
name: Centene Corporation
one_liner: Largest US Medicaid MCO, moat 4/10 — engine prints Tier B (weighted IRR 16.42%, IV@15% $77.51 vs $69.29) on an OCF base that capitalizes insurer working-capital/reserve timing, so the final tier is softened to C at low confidence; it clears 15% at ~$77.51 on engine numbers only, with a materially lower true margin of safety.
sector: Healthcare / Managed Care — Medicaid, ACA Marketplace & Medicare
tier_override_reason: Insurer model mismatch (same economics as SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH, not flagged only because Centene's sector is Healthcare, not Finance): the OCF-based OE base capitalizes premium/claims working-capital and reserve timing — TTM OE/share of $17.55 vs the $8.35 median base and guided FY2026 adjusted EPS above $4.80 shows the spread — and NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE is structural in 2023, 2024 and 2025, so tier-by-numbers B (16.42%, barely above the hurdle) overstates distributable owner's earnings; softened one notch to C, confidence low.
